locator: I q.2 a.3 co., secunda via: in omnibus causis efficientibus ordinatis, primum est causa medii, et medium est causa ultimi
interpretation: The per se ordering premise, read strongly and in parallel with the prima via's AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-SECOND-MOVERS-A: an efficient cause other than its effect that is itself efficiently caused is a middle cause, causing only as caused. 'Remota autem causa, removetur effectus' is read as the reason why the middle's causing depends on its cause. All predicates are present (simul), so a per accidens series of past generations (ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7) is not a counterexample. A weaker relevant-respect sibling reading, as for the prima via, is not yet formalized (candidate AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-SECUNDA-VIA-REMAINING).
